title: Prefix fingerprint coalescer and memory-aware dedup orchestration
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: the current prefix/KV cache stores many near-duplicate key-value fragments across requests and sessions. This wastes GPU memory, increases eviction churn, and reduces effective batch reuse. Goal: implement a lightweight, GPU-friendly fingerprint coalescer that deduplicates semantically identical or high-overlap prefix fragments across requests while being safe for streaming/continuous-batching. The feature must be memory-aware (prioritize coalescing where it yields net memory savings), low-latency (fingerprinting should add <1ms request overhead on hot paths), and compatible with existing fallback flows (fall back to per-request local KV if coalescer is unavailable).
acceptance_criteria: Reduce unique KV fragment storage by >= 45% in synthetic conversational workload (mix of template+user content)
End-to-end median request latency impact <= +2ms for steady-state workloads when coalescer is enabled
KV cache hit amplification: increase reused KV tokens per request by >= 30% compared to baseline
GPU memory used for prefix storage reduced by >= 20% on representative p4dn-like instance in canary tests
Safe rollback validated: system can disable coalescer at runtime without corrupting live KV caches or inflating evictions
technical_decision_log: Fingerprint format: 64-bit rolling Rabin hash over tokenized prefix segments (fast, low-collision) judged best tradeoff between speed and collision risk vs. heavier SHA variants
Global coalescer index: use per-GPU in-memory hash table with optional global Bloom filter for cross-GPU probed dedupe to avoid expensive network probes on hot paths
Eviction policy: 'memory-aware coalesce-first' where fragments that produce >1x memory saving when merged are prioritized; cheap heuristic uses fragment length + slot occupancy
Concurrency model: optimistic insert with compare-and-swap to attach existing fragment pointer; fallback path writes new fragment if CAS fails
Backcompat: store a 1-byte version tag in fragment metadata so older runtimes ignore coalesced entries; necessary for Mixed-version clusters (Hosted + Dedicated)
tasks: Design: finalize fingerprint format and collision testing harness
Runtime: implement per-GPU coalescer module and CAS attach API
Network: implement optional cross-GPU Bloom filter propagation via existing discovery channel
Eviction: extend slab allocator to account for coalesced-share factor
Testing: synthetic workload harness, perf bench, and canary in dedicated tier
Observability: add dashboard panels: coalescer hit rate, false-positive collisions, memory delta, and rollback drill
Docs: update KV cache architecture doc and runtime flags
comments: 2025-02-14 Sofia Patel: Created ticket after spike indicated 48% duplication in conversational read-heavy workload. Spike notes attached in Drive.
2025-02-18 Marco Nguyen: PoC of 64-bit rolling Rabin hashing finished; local microbench shows 350ns per fingerprint on x86 and ~700ns on our aarch64 nodes. Added benchmark results to PR.

2025-02-21 Elena Rivera (Review): Concern about bloom false positives leading to unnecessary probes; suggested storing small correction tag (8-bit) per fragment to reduce misresolution. Action: evaluate cost of correction tag vs extra probe.

2025-02-24 Marco Nguyen: Implemented per-GPU index + optional Bloom broadcast. Microbench: coalescer lookup adds 0.9ms P50 for end-to-end generation in continuous-batching mode. Memory regression test shows -22% prefix storage on p4dn-sim.

2025-02-26 Performance Team (notes): Observed increased eviction stalls under bursty workloads due to naive slab compaction. Mitigation: introduce 'coalesce-aware defragmenter' that packs coalesced fragments first. Added to tasks.

2025-02-28 QA: Canary started in Dedicated region eu-west-1 (subset of capacity). Initial telemetry: coalescer_hit_rate=0.62, collision_alerts=0, avg_reused_tokens_per_request +34%. No customer incidents.

2025-03-01 Marco Nguyen: Opened WIP PR for runtime changes (see PR link). Requesting design review from Storage and Scheduling teams. Next: add rollback path and run 72h dedicated canary before promoting to runtime-1.20 release branch.
notes: Tradeoffs considered: Heavy-weight content canonicalization (semantic hashing) rejected for now due to CPU cost and risk in hotspot paths; deferred to follow-up evaluation (ENG-???)
We must be conservative with cross-GPU probes to keep tail latencies low — Bloom filter approach reduces network queries at a small FP cost
Future work: explore quantized fingerprint storage in slab headers to further reduce per-fragment overhead and enable cross-instance replication of compact indices
